FILED s542r (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16, the round on main code cc36604b = MAIN-READY-95) from the companion ROW DIFF: t/op/fh.t swapped rows -- 2 "initial typeglob of file handle is undefined" and 5 "... not defined after increment" now PASS (they failed while `defined *{EXPR}` was always true), 3 "typeglob of file handle defined after select" and 7 "... defined after opening standard output" now FAIL.  Counts unchanged (6/2), so the snapshot never showed it; the row baseline did.

REPRO (scratch/s542r/probes/fhglob.pl in the s542r worktree; perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on main):

    $| = 1;
    my $a = "SYM000";
    print "2 initial:     ", (defined *{$a} ? "defined" : "undef"), "\n";   # perl undef    PCL undef
    select select $a;
    print "3 after select: ", (defined *{$a} ? "defined" : "undef"), "\n";  # perl defined  PCL undef
    $a++;
    print "5 incremented: ", (defined *{$a} ? "defined" : "undef"), "\n";   # perl undef    PCL undef
    open($a, ">&STDOUT") or die "open: $!";
    print "7 after open:  ", (defined *{$a} ? "defined" : "undef"), "\n";   # perl defined  PCL undef

WHY (read, not instrumented): #4301 (s532c) made `defined *{EXPR}` answer whether the glob EXISTS in the stash (p-glob-defined), which is perl's rule.  But a handle opened or selected through a SYMBOLIC name (a string in a scalar) is kept by the I/O layer without creating the stash glob that p-glob-defined looks up, so the glob still "does not exist" after `select $a` / `open($a, ...)` -- a silent wrong (the open itself works: row 6 "file handle used with open of standard output" passes, and writing through $a works).  In perl both operations vivify *main::SYM000.

SCOPE: the symbolic-name open / select paths (and probably `binmode`, `fileno`, `eof` on a name that is opened later); a bareword `open(FH, ...)` is the same question for `defined *FH` and is worth one probe.  The fix belongs where the I/O layer resolves a symbolic handle name: it should go through the same glob the stash holds, so every glob reader agrees (rule 11: one resolver), rather than a special case in p-glob-defined.

BASELINE: the two rows are keyed #5081 in baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv (s542r); rows 2 and 5 (keyed #1664) left by edit.  Related: #1664 (the typeglob model), #4301 (completed).

  -> perl defined, PCL undef.  Rows 2 and 5 agree; a BAREWORD `open(FH9, ...)` then `defined *FH9` -> defined in both.
  The two rows keyed here in baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv (op/fh.t 3 and 7) are this shape; not re-run.
LABEL: silent (already in the subject).

=== DONE (s543n, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24; WIP 1 7e5e8459) ===
A symbolic handle NAME is the glob of ITS package (unqualified: the package in effect, forced names main), CREATED
in that stash by an opener and by select: %p-install-fh's name arm files it under %p-name-handle-key (it was the :pcl
symbol, which no stash holds and every package's same short name found); `select "SYM"` vivifies the glob (a
present, empty IO entry) and keeps its FULL name, so a later print from another package reaches it.  op/fh.t's four
rows: `defined *{$a}` undef / defined after select / undef after $a++ / defined after open = perl.
